questions.prompt: Which HTTP status code should a server return when a request creates a new resource successfully?

options.explanation: 200 OK is for standard successful responses without resource creation.
201 Created indicates the request succeeded and a new resource was created, typically including a Location header.
204 No Content is for actions that succeed but produce no response body.
301 is a redirection status code.

questions.prompt: According to REST semantics, which HTTP method must be idempotent?

options.explanation: POST is typically non-idempotent because repeated calls create multiple resources.
PUT is strictly idempotent: making multiple identical PUT requests produces the exact same server state as a single request.
PATCH can be non-idempotent depending on the delta instruction.
CONNECT is used to establish tunnel connections.

questions.prompt: Why can an index on (last_name, first_name) NOT be used efficiently for the query `WHERE first_name = 'Alex'`?

options.text: Because B-Trees store data in descending order only.
options.explanation: B-Trees support bidirectional scans.

options.text: Due to the Leftmost Prefix Rule in composite B-Tree indexes.
options.explanation: Composite indexes can only be searched starting from the leftmost column (last_name). Filtering only on the second column forces a full scan of the index.

options.text: Because string comparisons cannot use B-Trees.
options.explanation: B-Trees are optimized for string ordering.

options.text: Because first_name is a reserved SQL keyword.
options.explanation: first_name is a standard identifier.

questions.prompt: Which isolation level prevents Dirty Reads and Non-Repeatable Reads, but may still permit Phantom Reads in standard SQL-92?

options.explanation: Allows dirty reads.
Allows non-repeatable reads.
Repeatable Read guarantees rows read cannot change during transaction, but new inserted rows (phantoms) may appear without range locks.
Serializable prevents all anomalies including phantoms.

questions.prompt: Which Redis data structure is optimal for maintaining a real-time leaderboard sorted by user scores with O(log N) insertion?

options.explanation: Hashes store field-value pairs without ordering.
Sorted Sets store elements ordered by score using skip lists and hash tables, supporting O(log N) updates and range queries.
Lists are ordered by insertion time, not score values.
HyperLogLog estimates cardinality of unique items.

questions.prompt: In the Cache-Aside (Lazy Loading) pattern, what happens when a read misses the cache?

options.text: The database writes to the cache directly.
options.explanation: The DB is unaware of the application cache.

options.text: The application reads from the DB, writes the result to cache, and returns it.
options.explanation: In Cache-Aside, the application queries the cache first. On a miss, it fetches from the primary DB, populates the cache, and serves the client.
The client receives the response synchronously from DB.

options.text: A background queue asynchronously refreshes all keys.
options.explanation: That describes Refresh-Ahead caching.

questions.prompt: What is the primary vulnerability of storing sensitive JWT access tokens in browser `localStorage`?

options.explanation: CSRF affects automatic cookie transmission, not manual Authorization headers.
Any injected JavaScript can access window.localStorage and exfiltrate the JWT. HttpOnly cookies protect against script access.
DNS poisoning is an infra network attack.
Local storage does not execute SQL.

questions.prompt: In Apache Kafka, what determines the maximum number of active consumers in a single consumer group that can process messages concurrently?

options.text: The number of broker nodes in the cluster.
options.explanation: Brokers host topics, but consumer parallelism is tied to partitions.
Each partition is consumed by exactly one consumer in a consumer group at any time. Extra consumers remain idle.

options.text: The total size of the message log in GB.
options.explanation: Log size does not limit consumer allocation.
The quorum manages metadata, not partition consumption limits.

questions.prompt: What will be the output of `bool([]) or (5 and 0)` in Python?

options.explanation: bool([]) is False, and (5 and 0) evaluates to 0.
bool([]) is False. In Python `False or X` returns X. `5 and 0` evaluates to 0 because 0 is falsy.
The expression returns the falsy value 0 itself.
None is not returned.

questions.prompt: What happens when using a mutable default argument like `def add_item(item, target_list=[])` in Python?

options.text: A new list is instantiated on every function call.
options.explanation: Default argument expressions are evaluated once when the function is defined.

options.text: The same list object persists across subsequent calls, causing unexpected mutations.
options.explanation: Python evaluates default parameters at definition time. Mutating target_list modifies the single shared object across all invocations.

options.text: Python raises a TypeError at runtime.
options.explanation: Mutable defaults are valid syntax.
Lists remain mutable.

questions.prompt: In CSS Flexbox, what does `justify-content: space-between` do?

options.text: Distributes items evenly along the cross axis.
options.explanation: The cross axis is aligned with align-content / align-items.

options.text: Places first item at start, last at end, with equal space between remaining items along main axis.
options.explanation: space-between anchors the extremities and divides available space evenly between interior items.

options.text: Adds equal margin before the first and after the last item.
options.explanation: That describes space-around or space-evenly.

options.text: Wraps overflowing items onto a new line.
options.explanation: Wrapping is controlled by flex-wrap.

questions.prompt: When does code following an `await` expression resume execution?

options.text: Synchronously in the same call stack turn.
options.explanation: Await always yields control back to the event loop.

options.text: In the microtask queue after the awaited Promise resolves.
options.explanation: Promise settlements schedule the continuation into the microtask queue, which drains before macrotasks (timers/I/O).

options.text: In a separate OS worker thread.
options.explanation: JavaScript execution is single-threaded.
Microtasks run immediately after the current script turn.

questions.prompt: Can a NumPy array of shape (4, 1) be broadcast with an array of shape (1, 3)? What is the resulting shape?

options.text: No, ValueError is raised because dimensions do not match.
options.explanation: Dimensions with length 1 are stretched to match.
Both trailing dimensions match rules (1 matches 3 -> 3, 4 matches 1 -> 4), resulting in a (4, 3) broadcast grid.
Shapes are not flattened.
Broadcasting expands dimensions, not shrinks them.

questions.prompt: In Pandas, what is the key difference between `df.loc[]` and `df.iloc[]`?

options.text: .loc is for rows only, .iloc is for columns only.
options.explanation: Both accept row and column indexers.

options.text: .loc is label-based (inclusive of slice end), while .iloc is integer position-based (exclusive of slice end).
options.explanation: .loc uses index/column labels and includes endpoint; .iloc uses 0-based integer positions and obeys standard Python exclusive slice rules.

options.text: .iloc supports boolean masks while .loc does not.
options.explanation: Both support boolean indexing.

options.text: .loc creates a deep copy, .iloc creates a view.
options.explanation: View/copy depends on memory layout, not accessor.
